{{Quote|Bacta can heal the body, but the Force can heal the soul.|A Jedi healer|<ref name="Threat of the Conqueror">{{SWGTCG|set=Threat of the Conqueror|cardname=Jedi Healer}}</ref>}}
'''Force healing''', '''Force heal''', or '''Cure''' was a [[Force power/Legends|power]] that used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to accelerate the natural healing process rapidly, and could be used to heal the most fatal of wounds and injuries.

==Applications==
{{Quote|Must relax&hellip; reach out with my mind&hellip; reach inside&hellip; through the pain&hellip; to touch the Force! Knit bones&hellip; mend flesh&hellip; renew!|[[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: Outlander">''[[Star Wars: Outlander]]''</ref>}}
Initial levels required meditation, but greater aptitude usually granted faster regeneration, without need of meditation. Greater levels of attainment were also able to mend far more severe injuries, even major damage to flesh and bone and even going as far as to mend internal damage, such as damage to the [[Heart/Legends|heart]], [[Lung/Legends|lungs]], and so forth; even to the point of sustaining functions of lost organs and on rare occasions resurrecting dead tissue or even persons.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

[[File:Force_Healing.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Meetra Surik]] using Force Heal.]]
A variation of this power was Force Purification, as well as Force Assist which was a Force technique that enabled the user to heal people other than themselves, and with enough concentration, the user was able to heal others' bodies and minds, simultaneously.

Although it was believed that malevolent Force-users could not employ Force healing, this was a wrong assumption. The [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] could in fact be used to heal, but, conjured from the dark side, such power often came at a terrible price. Additionally, some who primarily relied on the dark side were willing to use the light to heal, at least on occasion.<ref name="Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 4|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 4]]</ref>

A limit to some lasting dark side healing was the need to steal vitality from others. Often these powers were known as [[Force drain/Legends|Force Drain]] or Death Field.<ref name="Kotor">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>

Dark siders could use healing trances.<ref name=":2">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref>

==Users==
[[File:Force_heal_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Jedi, healing her own abdominal wound.]]
Practitioners were many, as were examples of its utilization: One [[Curato salva|version]] of this power merely undid fatigue and was expected to be used by all Jedi after the [[New Sith Wars]] until [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]].<ref name="Jedi Path" />

[[Jedi healer/Legends|Jedi healers]] used this power to diagnose and treat the ailments of their patients.

Decades before Sion, [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] was subject to somewhat similar healing when his shattered body was restored to wholeness after being crushed in the [[tomb of Freedon Nadd]]. It was unknown, though, whether this was the work of Kun himself or the spirit of [[Freedon Nadd]] himself working [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]]. This is made less clear due to the fact that some Sith magic could provide true healing, though often not as easily as a Jedi technique might.<ref name="Tales of the Jedi Companion">''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]''</ref>

Perhaps the most curious example of the dark side's cost of living is the case of the ancient Sith Lord [[Darth Sion]], the Lord of Pain. Sion could focus on his own pain and agony, using it to fuel the dark side and recover from grievous wounds nearly instantly. Sion's capability with this technique appeared almost perfect, but over time, his injuries accumulated to such a degree that he was in constant agony. This, however, he welcomed, as it fueled his power. To accomplish this task, he channeled the Force constantly to literally hold his shattered body together. Fortunately for Sion, it was very much a circular power: more pain beget more power, more power beget more capacity, more capacity beget more pain. Medical staff examining his body concluded that it should be pulling itself apart, so damaged was his physical shell. Sion died only when [[Meetra Surik]] [[Dun Möch/Legends|sowed doubt]] in Sion's mind, convincing him that his Force-dependent "life" was not worth existing.

[[File:BhatDying.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Anakin Skywalker trying to use Force healing on [[Bhat Jul]].]]
The most "benign", to the user at least, of these side effects was the healing being temporary, and requiring renewed applications or constant concentration to remain active. Among the dark side practitioners despite this discouraging result was [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]]. By focusing on the pain and anguish of others, he fueled the dark side and could sustain or invigorate himself. After being poisoned by the [[Brotherhood of Darkness/Legends|Brotherhood of Darkness]], he resorted to using this form of Force Healing to keep himself alive long enough to reach [[Caleb]], a true Force healer. This survival he accomplished by murdering a farmer's children before the man's eyes&mdash;the pain of the children's death coupled with their father's agony prior to his own death was enough to sustain Bane for hours. The Sith Lord would use this power periodically over his career despite his [[Orbalisk]] armor fulfilling a regenerative function.

[[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Darth Plagueis]], the master of Palpatine, also experimented with a dark side variant that would grant him the ability to create, maintain, or save life by manipulating [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|midi-chlorians]] to a certain degree. Plagueis stated that a child born of this power would be the embodiment of the Force. Although Sidious stated to Anakin that Plagueis had complete control over this ability, it is unknown whether he was in actuality successful in developing this. Regardless, Plagueis was able to over the course of years slowly impart true and lasting healing to many of his wounds and also had the power to resurrect the dead.<ref name=":1">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

[[File:BelandiFeearr-FDCR.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Belandi Feearr]], a Force-sensitive healer.]]
[[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Karness Muur|Murr]] uncovered the technique of Dark Transfer during his life. As such, [[Celeste Morne]] also knew how to apply the Force in this way.<ref name="Legacy 2006 30">[[Legacy (2006) 30|''Legacy'' (2006) 30]]</ref>

[[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]] used this Force power to heal a broken collar bone almost completely by meditation after the ambush of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba the Hutt's]] minions, during Mundi's mission to find [[Sharad Hett]].

Obi-Wan sustained his heart against weariness and age with the Force.<ref name="The Life and Legend of Obi-Wan Kenobi">''[[The Life and Legend of Obi-Wan Kenobi]]''</ref>

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] tried and initially failed to use this ability, much to his frustration.<ref name="The Clone Wars: Wild Space">''[[The Clone Wars: Wild Space]]''</ref> He later was able to resurrect [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]], but only by using the dying body of the [[Daughter/Legends|Daughter]] for more power.<ref name="Altar of Mortis episode">{{TCW|Altar of Mortis (episode)}}</ref> However, near the war's end, his healing skill was enough to ease anyone injured into a state of relaxation.<ref name="LoE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> Restoring dead tissue was a form used by Darth Vader, but was also utilized by the most skilled of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. Vader also experimented with Force healing fueled by the dark side, in which meditation on anger and frustration at his life and circumstances allowed his [[Lung/Legends|lungs]] to function without the aid of his [[Darth Vader's meditation chamber/Legends|hyperbaric chamber]] or his [[Darth Vader's armor/Legends|life support suit]]. He, too, quickly discovered that this application of dark side offered only a perversion of true healing, as the damaged alveoli of his lungs did not heal permanently, but rather remained functional as long as the intensity of his anger was kept focused. He only managed to maintain this power for a brief time, the pleasure he received from the healing process eventually breaking his concentration. Nevertheless, he was slowly able to expand the duration of his lungs' functionality, starting at a few seconds and gradually managing up to a few minutes. Vader's conclusion was that joy and happiness poisoned the dark side's power, and as such, they sabotaged the healing the technique afforded. However, he theorized that, with much practice and enormous willpower, he would eventually master the process and no longer be constricted by his life support system.<ref name="Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire novel">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

A notable case of this use of Force healing was [[Cilghal]] using the Force to cure [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] of a molecular poison that was incurable by conventional means, although, strictly speaking, the method of healing involved Cilghal's Force-powered [[Force sense/Legends|detection]] and [[Telekinesis/Legends|removal]] of the nanomachines afflicting Mon Mothma rather than a direct application of Force energy against the damaged cells themselves.<ref name="Champions of the Force">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref> Similarly, Anakin Solo once telekinetically clamped his wounds closed, when he would not take time to heal fully whilst leading a mission.<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Star by Star">''[[The New Jedi Order: Star by Star]]''</ref>

[[File:Mara_heals_trooper_TCG.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] using Force healing on a [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]].]]
At least some members of a [[Asogian/Legends|species]] native to [[Brodo Asogi]] possessed this technique, while the Jedi of the [[New Jedi Order]] used this ability in the form of a healing trance. Mara Jade was known to be able to fight through the pain she suffered by using a variant of the power that caused her to glow golden.<ref name=":0" /> After a lengthy and debilitating meditation, Luke Skywalker partly recovered from this trance by nearly immediately, resurrecting his own dead cells in preparation for combat.<ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Abyss">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Abyss]]''</ref>

Darth Caedus was known to have a version of healing that worked much as the Jedi version of simply causing his body to mend without needing to be constantly refreshed or stealing health from others, much like how [[Darish Vol]] could use the dark to heal himself enough to stay active in his old age.<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Revelation">''[[Legacy of the Force: Revelation]]''</ref><ref name="Fate of the Jedi: Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref>

[[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], also known as Palpatine, was capable of using the light side for Force healing, as was [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Darth Wyyrlok (III)|Wyyrlok]].<ref name="SagaCore">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref><ref name=":4">''[[Legacy Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

[[File:CadeHealingLightning-LECG.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Cade Skywalker uses his special form of Force healing.]]
[[Dark transfer]] was a rare variant of this Force power possessed by a descendant of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] named [[Cade Skywalker]].<ref name=":4" /> This power had the ability to bring others back from the brink of death, healing mortal wounds. His usage coincided with times of intense emotional distress. Cade believed he had to call upon the dark side in order to access the talent, but his former [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Wolf Sazen]] disputed this, believing that with proper training, the [[Light side of the Force/Legends|light side]] could accomplish such a feat as well, a position later proven correct.<ref name="Leg 46">[[Legacy (2006) 46|''Legacy'' (2006) 46]]</ref> The [[Sith Lord]] [[Darth Krayt]] also learned this ability and mastered it after combining knowledge from fellow user(s) [[Karness Muur]]/[[Celeste Morne]],<ref name="Legacy 2006 30">[[Legacy (2006) 30|''Legacy'' (2006) 30]]</ref> [[Darth Andeddu]], and Cade Skywalker, to the extent he was able to even heal himself from death, and when combined with the lightning he summoned, slay with a touch or return a corpse he laid hands upon to life.<ref name=":3">[[Legacy — War 6|''Legacy — War'' 6]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In games such as ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' and the [[Dark Forces/Jedi Knight|''Dark Forces''/''Jedi Knight'']] series, the player can give this power to the protagonists, to cure themselves and their party members of injuries or even poison. In the games, the usage of the power is often accompanied with some effects, like glowing swirls and sounds. These are believed to be more visual aids to the player, rather than an actual depiction of the power's behavior. However at least on occasion, in the wider Star Wars Media some versions of the power are known to have obvious visual effects,<ref name=":3" /> (beyond possibly closing the wounds of the user) such as causing the user to glow with golden light.<ref name=":0">''[[Dark Nest I: The Joiner King]]''</ref><ref name="Star Wars 1998 31">[[Star Wars (1998) 31|''Star Wars'' (1998) 31]]</ref>
